title: Chip stocks are getting hammered — but China's hottest new listing is holding up
excerpt: South Korean and Japanese semiconductor heavyweights lead a broad retreat as investors pulled back from big winners in the AI boom.
content_html:
By Huileng Tan

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Chip stocks sold off across Asia on Tuesday, with South Korean and Japanese semiconductor heavyweights leading a broad retreat as investors pulled back from some of the biggest winners of the AI boom.

South Korea's Kospi closed 11% lower after triggering its eighth circuit breaker this year. Index heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix ended 13% and 15% lower, respectively.

In Japan, the Nikkei 225 declined 4%. Memory-chip maker Kioxia — one of the market's standout performers in the first half of the year — slumped 18%.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. fell 3%, dragging the Taiex index down 5%.

Even China's CXMT Corp. wasn't entirely spared.

Shares in China's hottest new chip stock fell as much as 7.7% at the open before ending the day 4% lower. The pullback barely dented Monday's 466% debut surge, leaving the stock holding on to the vast majority of its gains.

CXMT's first-day rally gave it a market value of roughly 3.3 trillion yuan, or about $487 billion, making it the most valuable company listed on a mainland Chinese exchange. The blockbuster debut underscored investor enthusiasm for China's efforts to build a homegrown semiconductor industry.

China's chip push

That optimism is supported by expectations of a multi-year expansion in China's memory chip industry.

Official data released on Monday showed profits in the country's chipmaking sector surged more than 2,500% in the first half of the year.

Chinese memory-chip makers have significantly sped up their capacity-expansion plans for the next few years, Bernstein analyst Qingyuan Lin wrote in a Monday note.

"As the AI demand continues to grow and Nvidia continues to be banned by both Chinese and US government from shipping to China, we believe the advanced logic capacity expansion could further accelerate as well," Lin wrote.

The latest weakness in chip stocks also followed a report from "The Information" that a Chinese state-backed company has begun producing chipmaking machines domestically.

While the technology still trails the world's most advanced equipment, it marks another step in China's push to reduce its reliance on foreign suppliers and strengthen its semiconductor industry.

AI trade jitters

The broader chip selloff comes as investors grow more concerned about the huge amounts of money flowing into AI and the increasingly close financial ties among chipmakers, cloud providers, and AI developers.

The fear is that weakness in one part of the AI trade could quickly spread across the rest of the sector.

Those concerns weighed on Nvidia on Monday. Its shares fell about 5%, allowing Apple to overtake it as the world's most valuable publicly traded company.

周二，亚洲各地芯片股遭到抛售，韩国和日本半导体巨头领跌，投资者从人工智能热潮中的一些最大赢家撤资。

韩国综合股价指数在今年触发第八次熔断后收盘下跌 11%。 指数权重股三星电子和 SK 海力士分别下跌 13% 和 15%。

在日本，日经 225 指数下跌 4%。 内存芯片制造商 Kioxia 是今年上半年市场表现最出色的公司之一，股价下跌 18%。

台积电 下跌3%，拖累Taiex指数下跌5%。

即使是中国的长鑫存储也未能完全幸免。

中国最热门的新芯片股股价开盘下跌 7.7%，收盘下跌 4%。 此次回调几乎没有削弱周一首日涨幅 466% 的涨幅，使该股保住了大部分涨幅。

CXMT首日上涨使其市值约为3.3万亿元人民币（约合4870亿美元），使其成为中国大陆交易所市值最高的公司。 这一轰动一时的上市凸显了投资者对中国建设本土半导体产业的热情。

中国的芯片推动

这种乐观情绪得到了对中国存储芯片行业多年扩张的预期的支持。

周一公布的官方数据显示，上半年该国芯片制造行业利润飙升逾2,500%。

伯恩斯坦分析师林清源在周一的一份报告中写道，中国存储芯片制造商已大大加快了未来几年的产能扩张计划。

林写道：“随着人工智能需求持续增长，以及英伟达继续被中美政府禁止向中国发货，我们相信先进逻辑产能扩张也可能进一步加速。”

芯片股最近的疲软也是在《The Information》报道称一家中国国有企业已开始在国内生产芯片制造机器之后发生的。

尽管该技术仍落后于世界最先进的设备，但它标志着中国在减少对外国供应商的依赖并加强其半导体产业方面又迈出了一步。

人工智能贸易紧张

随着投资者越来越担心流入人工智能的巨额资金以及芯片制造商、云提供商和人工智能开发商之间日益密切的财务联系，芯片抛售范围也随之扩大。

人们担心人工智能行业某一部分的疲软可能会迅速蔓延到该行业的其他部分。

这些担忧周一给英伟达带来了压力。 其股价下跌约 5%，使苹果公司超越其成为全球市值最高的上市公司。
